messages:
incident-bot: Paging: High streaming tail latency observed in prod (us-west-2) across hosted API. Alert: p95 streaming latency > 2s for last 5m, error spike on chunk writes. Paging on-call. :rotating_light:

sara-eng-oncall: on it. I see the spike in the streaming lanes. Starting triage. Any customer-facing alerts yet?

raghu-sre: looking at infra metrics — GPU queues are saturated for long-tail users, KV cache miss rate up ~4x compared to baseline. Throughput steady but per-connection latency spikes.

kelly-prod: heads-up: two paying customers reported partial streaming failures to CS. Need quick mitigation if we toggle features. What's the blast radius of disabling streaming?

mike-platform: we can flip streaming off per-route via feature-flag for the hosted API at the gateway. Plan: target non-authenticated streaming routes first (low-risk) and shift them to chunked polling fallback. Canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 10m steps.

raghu-sre: agreed. Also propose rate-limiting long-lived SSEs > 30s and increasing prefix caching TTL to reduce KV misses while we stabilize.

sara-eng-oncall: @mike-platform do we have an emergency toggle script? I don't want manual console clicks.

deploy-bot: Available toggle: /deploy toggle-feature --name streaming_responses --scope hosted --cohort COHORT_ID --action disable --reason "mitigate streaming tail latency"

mike-platform: exact command i'll run in a sec. We'll target cohort: low-priority (cohort 11) first — mainly free-tier, anonymous, and experimental routes.

cs-lead: I'll notify the two impacted accounts and offer a status update. If we broaden to 25% they'll see degraded UX (no push), but responses still available via poll.

kelly-prod: add note for console metrics so customers know it's intentional. Also capture rollback plan.

raghu-sre: rollback: re-enable streaming and backfill caches; if latency returns, then we need to escalate to kernel-level batching or a temporary capacity bump.

sara-eng-oncall: okay executing canary now. @deploy-bot run the toggle command and log deployment id.

deploy-bot: Running: /deploy toggle-feature --name streaming_responses --scope hosted --cohort cohort-11 --action disable --reason "mitigate streaming tail latency"

ops-bot: Feature toggle applied to cohort-11 on hosted; deploy-id: 2026-1850012345-ff7. Observing metrics for 2m.

raghu-sre: initial effect: p95 streaming latency down ~18% for overall traffic, KV miss rate dropping. No spike in standard sync endpoints so far.

mike-platform: rolling to 25% (cohort-25) now. Command:
```
/deploy toggle-feature --name streaming_responses --scope hosted --cohort cohort-25 --action disable --reason "safety ramp"
```

deploy-bot: Applied to cohort-25; deploy-id: 2026-1850012360-a3c. Monitoring.

cs-lead: CS note posted: "We are temporarily disabling real-time streaming for a subset of requests to stabilize latency. All requests will still return responses via polling; we expect minimal data loss. We'll update you as we roll back." :white_check_mark:

raghu-sre: after 10m: p95 streaming latency now down 55% overall, tail error rate dropped ~70%. KV miss rate trending normalization. Looks promising.

kelly-prod: recommend holding at 25% for 20m and continue monitoring, notify legal/security if customers escalate.

sara-eng-oncall: agree. I'm keeping the page open and watching traces. If anything regresses, we'll revert cohort-25 and re-open targeted investigation.

mike-platform: plan for next steps: if stable at 25% -> 50% -> 100% with 10m gates. Also prepping a quota shift option: reduce concurrent-stream tokens per API key for free tier to reduce connection churn.

cs-lead: I'll prepare templated messages for customers if we need to expand more widely.

raghu-sre: one more mitigation: temporarily increase batching window for model X at the serving layer to improve kernel efficiency — low risk but could increase median latency slightly. Want approval to toggle if needed.

kelly-prod: approve conditional toggles. Prefer we keep median < 500ms. If batching pushes median beyond that, rollback.

sara-eng-oncall: note for post-incident: add a test in CI that simulates many long-lived streams to catch regressions earlier.

ops-bot: Metrics checkpoint at +30m: p95 latency stabilized, error rates normalizing. No new customer tickets beyond initial two.

mike-platform: moving to 50% now per rollout plan. /deploy toggle-feature --name streaming_responses --scope hosted --cohort cohort-50 --action disable --reason "ramp to stabilize"

deploy-bot: Applied to cohort-50; deploy-id: 2026-1850012440-b9d. Monitoring.

raghu-sre: at 50% we still see improved tail behavior. Proceeding to hold for 15m.

cs-lead: CS updated customers + public status page note drafted.

sara-eng-oncall: holding. If we get to 100% and everything stays green we'll plan to re-enable streaming with staggered rollout and extra cache warmup.

mike-platform: final step: if 100% re-enable, we'll do it in 5% increments and confirm KV cache hit rate holds. Also we'll lower default concurrent stream limits for free tier permanently until we ship a more robust KV sharding fix.

ops-bot: At +55m final check: p95 streaming latency back to baseline, error spike resolved. No further action recommended.

incident-bot: Incident update: High streaming tail latency — mitigated by staged disable of streaming responses for non-critical cohorts, rate shaping, and caching adjustments. Status: resolved (monitoring). Incident severity: Sev3.

kelly-prod: great work. Follow-ups: run retrospective, update rollout runbook with cohort toggling steps, and prioritize KV cache improvements for next quarter.

sara-eng-oncall: closing the page. If anyone sees regression reopen. Thanks team. :tada:
